title: Book of Our Fathers: Who’s Who Part 3

sense.text:
“For whatsoever things were written aforetime were written for our learning, that we through patience and comfort of the scriptures might have hope.” Every class starts here, because this is a Bible-based organization. The things that were written aforetime are this book, and they were written for us to learn from: what our forefathers went through, to give us hope at the end so we can make it through.

When Paul wrote this he was sending them into what we call today the Old Testament. All the books of the prophets, all the books the Most High God used to bring his people to the understanding, are important.

And there is a plot. There is a conspiracy against God's people, and that is the reason to go over the book of our fathers, because we have been disconnected. This is a book of our ancestors, a book of our forefathers and our foremothers, and it is through this book that we receive comfort. If we are patient and we endure and keep God's commandments and have faith in his son, we are going to receive all the things this book tells us we are going to receive. That is our faith. We are not here because we are a bunch of folks that want to hang out with each other. We are here because we all have a like mind, that we want to receive the kingdom of heaven, and in order to do that we must do what the Bible says.

“And thou, even thyself, shalt discontinue from thine heritage that I gave thee.” This is Jeremiah the prophet, and the Lord is telling him that even he is going to be cut off. That makes it a prophecy, so read it with purpose: who was cut off from the heritage God gave them? What people on the planet were disconnected from their true heritage, and why? When were the Israelites taken away from their God, their culture, their traditions, their laws? When were they removed from what God gave them? We are the only ones that fit that prophecy. The only ones on the face of the planet.

Read on and he says what he would do with us: “and I will cause thee to serve thine enemies in the land which thou knowest not.” We would be disconnected, and he would cause us to serve our enemies in a land we knew not.

“for ye have kindled a fire in mine anger, which shall burn for ever.” Which shall burn for ever. This happened because we upset the Father. We upset the Most High, and therefore he made good his word.

precepts.why:
“Therefore the Lord hath made good his word, which he pronounced against us.” He kept his end of the bargain. He told us exactly what was going to happen if we kept the commandments and what was going to happen if we did not, and the word he made good is Deuteronomy the 28th chapter.

Read on: “and against our judges that judged Israel, and against our kings, and against our princes, and against the men of Israel and Juda.” Against all of them, and what it brought was great plagues. All of those curses found in Deuteronomy the 28th chapter, verses 15 through 68, the Lord said he was going to do, and he did them. The curses were to be for a sign; they identify and show who the Israelites are. So put years and dates to it. When did those plagues come? When did those curses fall upon Israel? That is reading with purpose, and that is what they do not want us doing.

The world wants you to forget about Deuteronomy the 28th chapter. The nations want you to forget your history, and they go through great lengths to take you away from it, because there is connection when you get into your heritage. You start seeing that this correlates with what is going on with us right now, that this is the answer to our problems right now. Whenever we connect back to God, they know something is going to happen. Nobody ever asks why in Christianity it is so important to start at Matthew and not worry about the stuff beforehand. Because when you connect and correlate, something is going to happen.

And many of our people fall for the other thing instead, where the Bible is not really a big deal, where it is more superstition than a book you live by. You put the Bible on your dashboard so you would not get in a car accident. You hung the cross on the rearview, and it was supposed to bring power from God so the devil would not touch you in the car. How many accidents did you still have? You believed in that just as much as stepping on a crack breaking your mama's back. Throw salt, split the poles, see a black cat and take ten steps back. That held the same power to you as John 3:16. You were not religious, you were superstitious. You did not follow Christ.

sense.text:
“The ox knoweth his owner, and the ass his master's crib: but Israel doth not know, my people doth not consider.” Israel don't know. We are that people that don't know, nor do we consider.

Never did you ever think to open that book and search for heritage, because you fully bought into the white lies, the Edomite lies, that we are all the same people, that we are all created equal, and that we can all go to heaven together and hold hands. You bought into it so good that now as black folks you say it first: color doesn't matter, Jesus was all colors. You say it before master says it now.

There is a history that was taken away from us, and it is a fascinating story. When you read the scriptures you are going to see yourself. You are going to see how you are, your temperament, and why you move the way that you move. You are going to bear witness with a lot of historical figures that came and lived on this earth, and you are going to say, damn, that's my father right there. Read about Judah and it is your great great great up-teeth grandaddy. Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, that is your history.

They don't want us doing that, because when that happens self-worth comes in. You begin to consider. They want us dumb, dumber than animals, dumber than the ox that knows his master. Nations have gone through great lengths to hide your identity, and it is obvious now that you are awake, but our people that are asleep cannot see it. They cannot see all that is taking place to perpetuate the things that are done against us every day. So instead of looking and searching, we are distracted.

“Keep not thou silence, O God: hold not thy peace, and be not still, O God.” Then the reason: “For, lo, thine enemies make a tumult: and they that hate thee have lifted up the head.”

The enemies of God have made an uprising. The enemies of God are making an uproar. They that hate God have become prideful, they have become pompous. And what are they doing? Coming against God's people. They can't touch God. They can't reach up and throw a blow at God, so they come at the ones that they can touch, the ones they can throw a blow at.

“They have taken crafty counsel against thy people, and consulted against thy hidden ones.” Who are those hidden ones? The Israelites. This is where we have to read in between the lines, because when it says thy hidden ones it is going into our people with no sense of identity of who they are. They are hidden. Why? Because they don't have the Bible. They were cut off from their heritage.

And this is another thing they don't want us doing: taking accountability. Don't ever go for that nonsense where white folks say you're playing the race card. They know what time it is. They want you to live within the condition that you're in and not take accountability for what happened. They prefer you blaming them with no solutions, versus understanding what the true solution is and doing something about it. They'd rather you sit in the corner and be pissed off: man, look at my people, look how we living, we're the last hired and first fired, look at our jobs, look at our neighborhoods, our communities. You're just a complainer.

Versus the one that says, hold on, damn, this happened because we messed up. God said he was going to scatter us amongst the nations, and they didn't have nothing to do with that. That was us. But this is what happened when we went amongst them: they took advantage. They said, oh, now they've messed up, now we can strike and keep them down, now we can hold them underneath us.

“They have said, Come, and let us cut them off from being a nation; that the name of Israel may be no more in remembrance.” Cut them off from being a nation, a nationality, and get them while they're down, because if we cut them off, now the nations get to rule.

They went through great lengths to make sure that you don't remember you're the Jews. That you don't remember that you're an Ephraimite. That you don't remember that you're from the tribe of Manasseh, Simeon, Gad, Naphtali, Asher. To make sure you don't correlate your history and heritage with that book. Because if you do that, you might change the way that you think. You might change the way that you eat. You might change the way that you treat your neighbor.

“For they have consulted together with one consent: they are confederate against thee.” They are confederate against thee. This is not about somebody just having a good idea. They said, let us come together and figure out how we can get rid of these Israelites, how to remove them from their power forever, so we can take over. And there were things that they did, things that they put in place.

precepts.why:
“Wherefore the Israelites assembled themselves together, and came to Maspha, over against Jerusalem; for in Maspha was the place where they prayed aforetime in Israel.” This is going on during the time the Greeks are in control. We had been moved out; we weren't in the land to be able to do what we do. They had taken control over the temple and over the land, so we tried to come close and pray in a place that we used to pray at aforetime.

“Then they fasted that day, and put on sackcloth” — a sign of mourning — “and cast ashes upon their heads, and rent their clothes, And laid open the book of the law, wherein the heathen had sought to paint the likeness of their images.” Think about what the purpose would be. Somebody might read this and say they were just being disrespectful. No. Remember, it wasn't their book. It didn't belong to them. They opened up those books and started painting their own images in them, and left them there. The heathen went in and narrowed the noses. They saw our foremothers and narrowed the hips. They went through Egypt knocking the noses off the statues. They started coloring over the people. They made Isaiah, made Baruch, made all the prophets look a certain way, so that when you went back to that book you wouldn't correlate that this is your people.

Why is it important for you to change my history, to take away the look of my fathers and my mothers and make them look like you? It is for a reason, and it is by design. This is what came out of that crafty counsel. This is why the images are so important, and why Bishop Yawasap is always harping on imagery, because they know how the mind works. You see things enough, over and over and over, and you start to believe it. You start to think it's true. Now our people will literally damn near swear by Santa Claus, and all these fairy tales are somehow real. We like to play in the now; everything we do is for right now. Esau looked down the line. He's always done that.

“Hide me from the secret counsel of the wicked; from the insurrection of the workers of iniquity.” This is why David said it. That is the same crafty counsel of Psalms 83, where they came together against the hidden ones. They do things in secret, and he calls them workers of iniquity, workers of sin.

And their whole purpose is this: “That they may shoot in secret at the perfect: suddenly do they shoot at him, and fear not.” We are the perfect. That's why they do these things. That's why they put the images out there. That's why instead of Christ being a man of color, he's a Caucasian man. It is to shoot at the perfect in secret, so that you don't correlate your heritage to this Bible. And they don't fear when they do these things, because in their minds they think they are God.

“They search out iniquities; they accomplish a diligent search.” They search out these things. Okay, how can we keep these people destroyed? Esau thinks long term, and he accomplishes diligent searches to keep us destroyed.

“The earth is given into the hand of the wicked: he covereth the faces of the judges thereof.” He covers the faces of the judges thereof. What the wicked has done is hide, or try to hide, the true kings of this earth. He is trying to conceal and hold back the emergence of God's people. That is the big plot, and he is doing his best to hold it off as long as he can.

But Israel is busting out the seams now. You see the damage control happening, because they're confused about how we found out. So now that Israel is waking up and finding out, they're trying to control the information that goes out. You will see all manner of evil left up, but our stuff gets taken down; post something about the Israelites, tag IUIC, and all of a sudden it violates community standards. They are trying to filter it. Christianity and Islam are going back and forth with each other now, and it's up.

And a lot of them are tuned in. The class goes off and the bishop's evening class goes off with maybe seven or eight thousand people watching, and as soon as it's over the stream says thirty-five thousand watched. A lot of those people watching are these enemies. We think it's just us tuned in, and you've got five or six thousand of them watching, and right after we get done teaching they're saying, okay, look what he said. We have to be mindful of that too.

sense.text:
“Yea, and what have ye to do with me, O Tyre, and Zidon, and all the coasts of Palestine?” O Tyre and Zidon is talking about the sons of Ham. All the coasts of Palestine is talking about the sons of Ishmael. This prophecy is specific of the transatlantic slave trade, and it can be proved.

Go back in history and you have the sons of Ham, those people that appear black to you white folks, and the sons of Ishmael, who came against the Israelites to sell them. You had places like Fort Ouidah, Fort Judah, where we were sold. You also have places like Zanzibar where Ishmael was selling us. So you had Africans selling us and you had Ishmaelites selling us to white people that came on boats to the coast to pick us up.

“will ye render me a recompence? and if ye recompense me, swiftly and speedily will I return your recompence upon your own head.” That recompence is them trying to pay the Lord back, and the Lord says he will return their recompence upon their own head.

This is what the Amalekite was trying to say, and historically we already know about it. You're going to see a lot of white folks do the same thing: well, since you're talking about the slave trade, it was black people that sold black people. We know that, dummy. The Bible already told us. The problem is that you're trying to make it seem like those people were the same. They were not the same.

“Because ye have taken my silver and my gold, and have carried into your temples my goodly pleasant things.” They took God's silver and his gold, his treasures that were in the land and belonged to his people.

And they carried his goodly pleasant things into their temples. They took everything out of our temples and put it in theirs. They took our books, our writings, our historical things. They took everything that belonged to us and they took it for themselves.

“The children also of Judah and the children of Jerusalem have ye sold unto the Grecians.” This prophecy speaks specifically of the southern kingdom: the children of Judah and the children of Jerusalem, Benjamin and Levi. They took the southern kingdom and they sold them to the Grecians, to white people. So you had Hamites and Ishmaelites selling the Israelites to white people. That is the transatlantic slave trade. Yes, it happened.

The charge the Amalekite brought was this: that there is a growing consciousness amongst people of color in the Americas who likely descend from Israelite origins brought as slaves from Africa; that because of generations of trauma and loss of identity, along with the almost total rejection of this conversation amongst mainstream Jewish spaces, many black Hebrew Israelites get to the wrong conclusions and lash out at the Jewish people; that too many are coming from a very colonized Christian framework, using mistranslations of a mistranslated text from the King James Bible, and arriving at the false conclusion that mainstream Jews stole their identity; that it is a fact that a large percentage of the black slaves sold during the transatlantic slave trade were of Israelite tribes displaced in Africa, that over twenty percent of the slave trade consisted of Africans capturing an ethnic group in what is today called Nigeria and selling them to Europeans; and that it was not white people that went inland to take black slaves, it was other black African leaders who took certain groups of people in Africa and sold them to the whites on the coast. And he said his team is actively working on a documentary series.

They only accept it when they say it. If we say it before them, no, it's a lie, it's made up, you're stealing identity. But if they say it first, then okay, you are who we say you are. And the book brought up on the screen debunks the rest of it: the Jews were the largest ship chandlers in the entire Caribbean region, where the shipping business was mainly a Jewish enterprise, trading and serving as merchants, owning warehouses with inventories to outfit the largest selling vessels and to make ship repairs. They were part of the slave trade. He claimed we were the same people — well, if you're a Jewish brother, why would you be against it? Did they bear witness with us when they came? No.

So what his team is actively working on is to confuse the people of God. And think about it: what sparked them to go back and say there are Israelites in Africa? What brought them to that conclusion? We ain't stupid. We didn't need no validation from any other nation. We don't need no validation from nobody but the Most High God and his son. That's who we got it from. Before you were forced to say it, we had already found it out; the cat was already out the bag. Now you're trying to control the information and lead our people away from Christ, to sift them away from the Lord and make them Old Testament only. You're not taking us there. We are not joining you hand in hand in that nonsense you believe in. Period. All praise be to the Most High God and his son for visions, and for this truth and this word.

“And whilst they sinned not before their God, they prospered, because the God that hateth iniquity was with them.” Don't ever be confused: this right here is their fear. Their fear is our compliance with the Most High God. That is terrifying to them.

Forget about all the glitz and glam. You can get out there and get a thousand people to kiss your boot and you are not a threat. Get two or three Israelites to repent and keep the commandments and they're trying to take you off the map. They're going to slander your name. They're going to drag you. Get them to repent and believe on Christ and see what happens.

“But when they departed from the way which he appointed them, they were destroyed in many battles very sore, and were led captives into a land that was not their's, and the temple of their God was cast to the ground, and their cities were taken by the enemies.” That is the pattern they watched: when we departed, we were destroyed and carried captive, the temple cast down and the cities taken. “But now are they returned to their God, and are come up from the places where they were scattered, and have possessed Jerusalem, where their sanctuary is, and are seated in the hill country.”

“Now therefore, my lord and governor, if there be any error against this people, and they sin against their God, let us consider that this shall be their ruin, and let us go up, and we shall overcome them.” They said, let us consider that this is going to be their ruin. If they sin against the Most High, now we can move on them. But if they're not in the midst of sin, then we're going to get done like them Egyptians.

We read this and we read it on the surface, but this is a generational study of the Israelites. This was generations of seeing how we were destroyed over the years. This was a study on us. They knew generationally that this is how our people are, and that is how he knew exactly how we deal. When they're with the Lord, when they're keeping the commandments, the Lord is with them and we can't touch them. But when they're in the midst of sin, we got them.

They studied us for centuries. That is the diligent search, years of observation.

This is Joshua. It says Jesus because it is the same name, and it has the same meaning: Yeshua, Yehoshua, Jesus, all the same thing.

He “was valiant in the wars, and was the successor of Moses in prophecies, who according to his name was made great for the saving of the elect of God, and taking vengeance of the enemies that rose up against them, that he might set Israel in their inheritance.” Made great for the saving of the elect of God, and he was the one who was going to set Israel in their inheritance.

Joshua was from the tribe of Ephraim, and he was likely born around 1485 BC, in Egypt. These are approximates.

precepts.why: “Of the tribe of Ephraim, Oshea the son of Nun.” That settles the tribe. Joshua was from the tribe of Ephraim, and Oshea the son of Nun is the same name as Joshua.

“These are the names of the men which Moses sent to spy out the land. And Moses called Oshea the son of Nun Jehoshua.” Moses himself changed it, and Jehoshua is the same name again.

“And Moses sent them to spy out the land of Canaan, and said unto them, Get you up this way southward, and go up into the mountain.” They were sent to see the land, what it is, and the people that dwell in it, whether they be strong or weak, few or many; what the cities are, whether in tents or in strongholds; and whether the land be fat or lean, and whether there be wood therein or not. So Joshua was one of the ones that was sent to spy out this land.

Out of that whole generation, who made it out of Egypt? All those that were twenty and under, and Joshua and Caleb. “Doubtless ye shall not come into the land, concerning which I sware to make you dwell therein, save Caleb the son of Jephunneh, and Joshua the son of Nun.”

“But your little ones, which ye said should be a prey, them will I bring in, and they shall know the land which ye have despised. But as for you, your carcases, they shall fall in this wilderness.” That is how the Lord deals. We don't want the Lord to get involved when he wants to fix us, because you see how he fixes things.

“Now after the death of Moses the servant of the Lord it came to pass, that the Lord spake unto Joshua the son of Nun, Moses' minister, saying, Moses my servant is dead; now therefore arise, go over this Jordan, thou, and all this people, unto the land which I do give to them, even to the children of Israel.” So it was Joshua that was going to be the one to take them over.

Put things into perspective and you see why he had to be told to have good courage. Consider all the people that had just died, and what he was about to take on. Israel was rebellious. Israel was stiffnecked. All that you've seen and been through, and now you've got to accomplish this. Imagine sitting in that seat of leadership, being over a nation. Some brothers become officers of ten and feel like that's so much responsibility; a brother becomes a twenty, a fifty. Imagine being over the nation, and literally not knowing what you're stepping into. If you've ever led somebody through the woods, you know: you make the wrong move and everybody dies. He had seen all that took place, how the firstborn died, and he was part of that generation. All his friends, all his people, all the folks he looked up to as elders, they couldn't go. You get to this new place and you might be next. The Lord wasn't playing. That is the amount of pressure that was on his shoulders, and he took up the mantle.

“Every place that the sole of your foot shall tread upon, that have I given unto you, as I said unto Moses. From the wilderness and this Lebanon even unto the great river, the river Euphrates, all the land of the Hittites, and unto the great sea toward the going down of the sun, shall be your coast.” This is not some small piece he could see from where he stood. This is a great land mass that the Lord is telling them is going to be theirs.

“There shall not any man be able to stand before thee all the days of thy life: as I was with Moses, so I will be with thee: I will not fail thee, nor forsake thee. Be strong and of a good courage: for unto this people shalt thou divide for an inheritance the land, which I sware unto their fathers to give them.” Be strong and of a good courage, because in order to stand in his seat he was going to have to have these attributes. In any seat of leadership you have to be strong. You're going to get hit with stuff that doesn't even belong to you. Things are going to come your way that you have absolutely no control over, and it's still your responsibility to get it taken care of and get it rectified. That's the seat of a leader. Israel will stretch you out.

And understand what the Lord is telling him: this land is yours. There were people inhabiting that land. Joshua wasn't like the leaders and presidents we think of, who aren't boots on the ground. When you're with the Lord, we're in the fight. Joshua was in the army. He was in that military. All that the Lord said was going to be his was going to be his, but he had to go get it, and the Lord said don't be afraid, I'm with you.

Moses knew this, because the Lord had told Moses he wasn't going to see it. “And Moses called unto Joshua, and said unto him in the sight of all Israel, Be strong and of a good courage: for thou must go with this people unto the land which the Lord hath sworn unto their fathers to give them; and thou shalt cause them to inherit it.”

And the promise with it: the Lord it is that doth go before thee, he will be with thee, he will not fail thee, neither forsake thee. So it was Joshua that succeeded Moses.

“Now Jericho was straitly shut up because of the children of Israel: none went out, and none came in.” That was martial law, by the Hittites and the Canaanites. He had it shut down.

“And the Lord said unto Joshua, See, I have given into thine hand Jericho, and the king thereof, and the mighty men of valour.” The Lord gave him the king of Jericho and the mighty men of valour. “And ye shall compass the city, all ye men of war, and go round about the city once. Thus shalt thou do six days.” Surround the city, all you men of war. “And seven priests shall bear before the ark seven trumpets of rams' horns: and the seventh day ye shall compass the city seven times, and the priests shall blow with the trumpets. And it shall come to pass, that when they make a long blast with the ram's horn, and when ye hear the sound of the trumpet, all the people shall shout with a great shout; and the wall of the city shall fall down flat, and the people shall ascend up every man straight before him.”

This Bible is a war book. People talk about praying like the battle of Jericho, but read it: “And he said unto the people, Pass on, and compass the city, and let him that is armed pass on before the ark of the Lord.” Let him that is armed. This wasn't a prayer team. These weren't prayer warriors. “And the armed men went before the priests that blew with the trumpets, and the rereward came after the ark, the priests going on, and blowing with the trumpets. And Joshua had commanded the people, saying, Ye shall not shout, nor make any noise with your voice, neither shall any word proceed out of your mouth, until the day I bid you shout; then shall ye shout.” The Israelites was kicking ass.

“So the people shouted when the priests blew with the trumpets: and it came to pass, when the people heard the sound of the trumpet, and the people shouted with a great shout, that the wall fell down flat, so that the people went up into the city, every man straight before him, and they took the city.”

They took the city. They didn't pray the city into their hands. “And they utterly destroyed all that was in the city, both man and woman, young and old, and ox, and sheep, and ass, with the edge of the sword.” The brakes were off of him that day. Everybody got to work, in the name of the Lord.

This is where so-called Christians get uncomfortable. There's no reason to get uncomfortable about it. Think about it: my ancestors did this. My fathers did this.

Joshua was one of the twelve spies who trusted God. “And Joshua the son of Nun, and Caleb the son of Jephunneh, which were of them that searched the land, rent their clothes: And they spake unto all the company of the children of Israel, saying, The land, which we passed through to search it, is an exceeding good land. If the Lord delight in us, then he will bring us into this land, and give it us; a land which floweth with milk and honey.”

This is them speaking, and they were young men at the time. Some of the Israelites, let's be honest, their faith was weak; they were old and they weren't with the business like that. But Joshua and Caleb had faith. “Only rebel not ye against the Lord, neither fear ye the people of the land; for they are bread for us: their defence is departed from them, and the Lord is with us: fear them not.” He said, y'all don't be afraid.

But watch what it got them: “But all the congregation bade stone them with stones. And the glory of the Lord appeared in the tabernacle of the congregation before all the children of Israel. And the Lord said unto Moses, How long will this people provoke me? and how long will it be ere they believe me, for all the signs which I have shewed among them? I will smite them with the pestilence, and disinherit them, and will make of thee a greater nation and mightier than they.” That is how the Lord deals.

This is one many of us quote, because this was the temperament of Joshua. After they had conquered the Canaanites, he is exhorting the people: “And if it seem evil unto you to serve the Lord, choose you this day whom ye will serve; whether the gods which your fathers served that were on the other side of the flood, or the gods of the Amorites, in whose land ye dwell.”

Pick a side. There wasn't no in between. Then he picks his own: “but as for me and my house, we will serve the Lord.” We're going to serve the Lord.

Joshua died at a hundred and ten years old. “And it came to pass after these things, that Joshua the son of Nun, the servant of the Lord, died, being an hundred and ten years old.”

Look at his life. Born in Egypt, he went through all of that and saw all the plagues that hit Egypt. Then he lived through the wilderness and saw all the rebellion happen. This is why he wasn't playing; he said we've got to have faith, we can't fear, we can't make the same mistake.

And he gets throughout his life and sees the Lord deliver Israel and give them the land. Joshua was there for all of that. When the land got divided up, Joshua was there. That land that was promised to our fathers, that flowed with milk and honey, Joshua got to see it. He got to see what Moses didn't get to see, and it's all because he remained faithful.

This is how Joshua rolled. “Surely none of the men that came up out of Egypt, from twenty years old and upward, shall see the land which I sware unto Abraham, unto Isaac, and unto Jacob; because they have not wholly followed me.” They have not wholly followed me. They had some doubt in them; they lacked faith somewhere.

But who didn't? “Save Caleb the son of Jephunneh the Kenezite, and Joshua the son of Nun: for they have wholly followed the Lord.” They had complete faith. Whatever the Lord told Moses and Moses told them, they didn't doubt. When they went to spy out the land, Joshua was saying, hey, we can take this place; it don't matter how big they are, it don't matter how high the walls of Jericho are, we can take this place.

That is the same spirit that we've got to roll in, that we follow the Lord wholly without doubt. That's what he wants from us.

“And they buried him in the border of his inheritance in Timnath–serah, which is in mount Ephraim, on the north side of the hill of Gaash.” They buried him in his own land.

“And Israel served the Lord all the days of Joshua, and all the days of the elders that overlived Joshua, and which had known all the works of the Lord, that he had done for Israel.” That speaks of his leadership. Deacon Malachi says it a lot, that great leaders create more great leaders, and we're seeing that in the time that Israel served the Lord under Joshua. The men of Joshua were raised up underneath him, and they rolled in the same spirit. That's why it says Israel served the Lord all the days of Joshua, and all the days of the elders that overlived Joshua.

“And the bones of Joseph, which the children of Israel brought up out of Egypt, buried they in Shechem, in a parcel of ground which Jacob bought of the sons of Hamor the father of Shechem for an hundred pieces of silver.” All praise to the Most High. Give it up for our forefather Joshua, son of Nun.

sense.text:
Joshua was with the business. “And with hailstones of mighty power he made the battle to fall violently upon the nations, and in the descent of Beth-horon he destroyed them that resisted.” He was in many wars; he fought many battles.

“that the nations might know all their strength, because he fought in the sight of the Lord, and he followed the Mighty One.” He followed the Mighty One, and that is why the nations came to know their strength.

“In the time of Moses also he did a work of mercy, he and Caleb the son of Jephunne, in that they withstood the congregation, and withheld the people from sin, and appeased the wicked murmuring.” He and Caleb the son of Jephunneh, the two of them together, withstood the congregation and withheld the people from sin.

“And of six hundred thousand people on foot, they two were preserved to bring them in to the heritage, even unto the land that floweth with milk and honey.” Out of six hundred thousand on foot, two were preserved, and they were the two to bring the people in to the heritage.

“The Lord gave strength also unto Caleb, which remained with him unto his old age: so that he entered upon the high places of the land, and his seed obtained it for an heritage.” Caleb was an example, and it is going to be very similar with Joshua, because it was around the same time.

Caleb was from the tribe of Judah, he was born in Egypt, and we allot him the same birth year as Joshua, around 1485 BC, because it doesn't specifically state when.

precepts.why: “Of the tribe of Judah, Caleb the son of Jephunneh.” That is the tribe. This is Caleb the son of Jephunneh, from the tribe of Judah.

He is often called Caleb the son of Jephunneh, the Kenizzite. “Then the children of Judah came unto Joshua in Gilgal: and Caleb the son of Jephunneh the Kenezite said unto him, Thou knowest the thing that the Lord said unto Moses the man of God concerning me and thee in Kadesh–barnea.”

This is the same person. This is the same Caleb. Sometimes when we're reading in the Old Testament and the names come differently, you think they're different people; it's talking about the same person.

“And Joshua blessed him, and gave unto Caleb the son of Jephunneh Hebron for an inheritance. Hebron therefore became the inheritance of Caleb the son of Jephunneh the Kenezite unto this day, because that he wholly followed the Lord God of Israel.”

Hebron was his portion, and the reason given is the same reason again: because he wholly followed the Lord God of Israel. He was also one of the spies who trusted God.

“And Moses sware on that day, saying, Surely the land whereon thy feet have trodden shall be thine inheritance, and thy children's for ever, because thou hast wholly followed the Lord my God.” This is Caleb speaking of what Moses swore to him.

“And now, behold, the Lord hath kept me alive, as he said, these forty and five years, even since the Lord spake this word unto Moses, while the children of Israel wandered in the wilderness: and now, lo, I am this day fourscore and five years old. As yet I am as strong this day as I was in the day that Moses sent me: as my strength was then, even so is my strength now, for war, both to go out, and to come in.” Fourscore and five years old with the same strength he had in his youth. That is the kind of man Caleb was.

But here is the thing to pick out for the book of our fathers: he didn't retain that strength just to walk around in small t-shirts saying he's swole. What was the reason he said the Lord gave him that strength? War. The Lord gave me this strength to fight with. So give me some land, because I'm still fighting for this Lord. I ain't retired from battle. Eighty-five years old out there whooping ass. He beat the brakes off them Hamites. Imagine them seeing this old man moving around like that; they'd think surely these are gods on earth.

“Now therefore give me this mountain, whereof the Lord spake in that day; for thou heardest in that day how the Anakims were there, and that the cities were great and fenced: if so be the Lord will be with me, then I shall be able to drive them out, as the Lord said.” And he got it: “And Joshua blessed him, and gave unto Caleb the son of Jephunneh Hebron for an inheritance.” The name of Hebron before was “Kirjath–arba; which Arba was a great man among the Anakims. And the land had rest from war.”

“And the Lord said, I have pardoned according to thy word: But as truly as I live, all the earth shall be filled with the glory of the Lord.”

“Because all those men which have seen my glory, and my miracles, which I did in Egypt and in the wilderness, and have tempted me now these ten times, and have not hearkened to my voice; Surely they shall not see the land which I sware unto their fathers, neither shall any of them that provoked me see it.” Ten times. The Lord don't lie, and he ain't playing.

Then the exception: “But my servant Caleb, because he had another spirit with him, and hath followed me fully, him will I bring into the land whereinto he went.” He had another spirit with him. He wasn't like them. We saw it already, where the two spies were exhorting the older Israelites that we've got to have faith. We have to have a different spirit. There has got to be something different about you in regards to faith. You can't move in that faithless spirit; it's not going to get us anywhere, it's not going to profit us at all.

And remember Romans 15 and 4: through patience and comfort of the scriptures we have hope, and the things written aforetime were written for our learning. Read about Caleb and it's, shoot, that's how I've got to move. I've got to have that mindset. I've got to fully trust in God and follow him regardless of what everybody else is doing, regardless of the peer pressure, regardless of what other folks have going on, the tribulations, whatever trial comes my way, whatever temptation comes at me. I've got to follow no matter what. That's how Caleb moved, and he was rewarded because of it.

This is him going to get his land. “And the west border was to the great sea, and the coast thereof. This is the coast of the children of Judah round about according to their families. And unto Caleb the son of Jephunneh he gave a part among the children of Judah, according to the commandment of the Lord to Joshua, even the city of Arba the father of Anak, which city is Hebron.”

“And Caleb drove thence the three sons of Anak, Sheshai, and Ahiman, and Talmai, the children of Anak. And he went up thence to the inhabitants of Debir: and the name of Debir before was Kirjath–sepher. And Caleb said, He that smiteth Kirjath–sepher, and taketh it, to him will I give Achsah my daughter to wife.”

He was promised Hebron, and he went to go claim it.

Here is who was in the land: “The Amalekites dwell in the land of the south: and the Hittites, and the Jebusites, and the Amorites, dwell in the mountains: and the Canaanites dwell by the sea, and by the coast of Jordan.”

“And Caleb stilled the people before Moses, and said, Let us go up at once, and possess it; for we are well able to overcome it.” For we are well able to overcome it. Caleb weren't no punk.

“But the men that went up with him said, We be not able to go up against the people; for they are stronger than we.” You can't stand folks like this, and you can't have folks like this in your circle. “And they brought up an evil report of the land which they had searched unto the children of Israel, saying, The land, through which we have gone to search it, is a land that eateth up the inhabitants thereof; and all the people that we saw in it are men of a great stature. And there we saw the giants, the sons of Anak, which come of the giants: and we were in our own sight as grasshoppers, and so we were in their sight.”

That is who Caleb went up and took his land from. Truly, he was with the business. They was giants, and this is an eighty-five-year-old saying, listen, we are well able, we straight. Give it up for our forefather Caleb.

sense.text:
“The Lord gave strength also unto Caleb, which remained with him unto his old age.” That is why he was that way. The Lord gave him that strength. Everybody don't get that.

And you know when you have strength: it is whenever you fall. Don't think strength is present when everything is good and gravy. It's when you're going through something. That's when your strength is shown.

“so that he entered upon the high places of the land, and his seed obtained it for an heritage.” What Caleb's seed obtained was Hebron, the land that was given to him.

“That all the children of Israel might see that it is good to follow the Lord.” That is what Caleb's whole life was for: so that all the children of Israel might see that it is good to follow the Lord.

“And concerning the judges, every one by name, whose heart went not a whoring, nor departed from the Lord, let their memory be blessed.” It says concerning the judges, every one by name, so the names are what we go after: Othniel, Ehud, Shamgar, Deborah, Gideon, Tola, Jair, Jephthah, Ibzan, Elon and Abdon.

precepts.why:
The first one by name is Othniel. “And the children of Israel did evil in the sight of the Lord, and forgat the Lord their God, and served Baalim and the groves. Therefore the anger of the Lord was hot against Israel, and he sold them into the hand of Chushan–rishathaim king of Mesopotamia: and the children of Israel served Chushan–rishathaim eight years.” Eight years they served him.

“And when the children of Israel cried unto the Lord, the Lord raised up a deliverer to the children of Israel, who delivered them, even Othniel the son of Kenaz, Caleb's younger brother.” He was a son of Kenaz, Caleb's younger brother. That is the connection back to Caleb.

“And the Spirit of the Lord came upon him, and he judged Israel, and went out to war: and the Lord delivered Chushan–rishathaim king of Mesopotamia into his hand; and his hand prevailed against Chushan–rishathaim. And the land had rest forty years. And Othniel the son of Kenaz died.”

The second one is Ehud. “And the children of Israel did evil again in the sight of the Lord: and the Lord strengthened Eglon the king of Moab against Israel, because they had done evil in the sight of the Lord. And he gathered unto him the children of Ammon and Amalek, and went and smote Israel, and possessed the city of palm trees. So the children of Israel served Eglon the king of Moab eighteen years.”

There is so much to uncover in this. We had many captivities, and there is not one nation that ain't got something to pay for. While y'all want to hold hands and sing Kumbaya, all nations play a part unto this day in our demise.

“But when the children of Israel cried unto the Lord, the Lord raised them up a deliverer, Ehud the son of Gera, a Benjamite, a man lefthanded.” Here is the point: Ehud was one of the judges, number two, he was left-handed, and he was from the tribe of Benjamin.

“So Moab was subdued that day under the hand of Israel. And the land had rest fourscore years.” There is a lot of history skipped in between, so don't think this is covering everything; there is a lot in chapter 3.

“And after him was Shamgar the son of Anath, which slew of the Philistines six hundred men with an ox goad: and he also delivered Israel.” So this was another one, Shamgar, and he killed six hundred with an ox goad.

The goad is a formidable weapon, sometimes ten feet long with a sharp point. That wasn't no slingshot. Six hundred folks died by one of them.

“And Deborah, a prophetess, the wife of Lapidoth, she judged Israel at that time.” This was the only woman judge.

“And she dwelt under the palm tree of Deborah between Ramah and Beth–el in mount Ephraim: and the children of Israel came up to her for judgment.” She was a wise woman, and Israel respected her; they came up to her for judgment.

She was one of the ones that had to rise up when brothers weren't handling business. All praises for our foremothers that stood up.

“And the children of Israel did evil in the sight of the Lord: and the Lord delivered them into the hand of Midian seven years. And the hand of Midian prevailed against Israel: and because of the Midianites the children of Israel made them the dens which are in the mountains, and caves, and strong holds.”

“And so it was, when Israel had sown, that the Midianites came up, and the Amalekites, and the children of the east, even they came up against them; And they encamped against them, and destroyed the increase of the earth, till thou come unto Gaza, and left no sustenance for Israel, neither sheep, nor ox, nor ass. For they came up with their cattle and their tents, and they came as grasshoppers for multitude; for both they and their camels were without number: and they entered into the land to destroy it. And Israel was greatly impoverished because of the Midianites; and the children of Israel cried unto the Lord.”

And the Lord answered the cry with a word first: “Thus saith the Lord God of Israel, I brought you up from Egypt, and brought you forth out of the house of bondage; And I delivered you out of the hand of the Egyptians, and out of the hand of all that oppressed you, and drave them out from before you, and gave you their land; And I said unto you, I am the Lord your God; fear not the gods of the Amorites, in whose land ye dwell: but ye have not obeyed my voice.”

Then comes the judge: “And there came an angel of the Lord, and sat under an oak which was in Ophrah, that pertained unto Joash the Abi–ezrite: and his son Gideon threshed wheat by the winepress, to hide it from the Midianites. And the angel of the Lord appeared unto him, and said unto him, The Lord is with thee, thou mighty man of valour.” Thou mighty man of valour. This is Gideon.

“And Gideon said unto him, Oh my Lord, if the Lord be with us, why then is all this befallen us? and where be all his miracles which our fathers told us of, saying, Did not the Lord bring us up from Egypt? but now the Lord hath forsaken us, and delivered us into the hands of the Midianites.” To read more on Gideon, read chapters 6 through 8.

“And after Abimelech there arose to defend Israel Tola the son of Puah, the son of Dodo, a man of Issachar; and he dwelt in Shamir in mount Ephraim.” A man of Issachar.

“And he judged Israel twenty and three years, and died, and was buried in Shamir.” That is Tola.

“And after him arose Jair, a Gileadite, and judged Israel twenty and two years.” The next judge is Jair.

“And he had thirty sons that rode on thirty ass colts, and they had thirty cities, which are called Havoth–jair unto this day, which are in the land of Gilead.” They called him that because that is where he was from.

“Now Jephthah the Gileadite was a mighty man of valour, and he was the son of an harlot: and Gilead begat Jephthah. And Gilead's wife bare him sons; and his wife's sons grew up, and they thrust out Jephthah, and said unto him, Thou shalt not inherit in our father's house; for thou art the son of a strange woman. Then Jephthah fled from his brethren, and dwelt in the land of Tob.”

And he was a judge. We all have backgrounds, so don't think the Lord can't use who he wants to use.

“And they said unto Jephthah, Come, and be our captain, that we may fight with the children of Ammon.”

And Jephthah didn't forget: “And Jephthah said unto the elders of Gilead, Did not ye hate me, and expel me out of my father's house?” To read more on Jephthah, read chapters 11 and 12.

“And after him Ibzan of Beth–lehem judged Israel.” The next one is Ibzan.

“And he had thirty sons, and thirty daughters, whom he sent abroad, and took in thirty daughters from abroad for his sons.” Thirty sons and thirty daughters.

“And after him Elon, a Zebulonite, judged Israel; and he judged Israel ten years.” Elon is another judge, and he judged Israel for ten years.

“And Elon the Zebulonite died, and was buried in Aijalon in the country of Zebulun.” So we had another judge from the tribe of Zebulun.

“And after him Abdon the son of Hillel, a Pirathonite, judged Israel.” The next is Abdon.

“And he had forty sons and thirty nephews, that rode on threescore and ten ass colts: and he judged Israel eight years.” Forty sons. Give it up for the judges.

sense.text:
“And concerning the judges, every one by name, whose heart went not a whoring, nor departed from the Lord, let their memory be blessed.” Let their memory be blessed.

“Let their bones flourish out of their place, and let the name of them that were honoured be continued upon their children.” Let their bones flourish out of their place, and let the name of them that were honoured be continued upon their children. Give it up for the judges.

“Samuel, the prophet of the Lord, beloved of his Lord, established a kingdom, and anointed princes over his people.” This is Samuel, son of Elkanah, and his mother's name was Hannah.

He anointed princes, and he anointed both kings. Estimated time of birth, around 1,100 BC. He was from Ramathaim of mount Ephraim, which is where we note him being from, because that is basically where they were at; when it says Ramah, that is the same area.

“By the law of the Lord he judged the congregation, and the Lord had respect unto Jacob.” By the law of the Lord he judged the congregation. He was considered the last judge of Israel, because after him came King Saul, and after that we went into kingship.
“By his faithfulness he was found a true prophet, and by his word he was known to be faithful in vision.” Found a true prophet by his faithfulness, and known to be faithful in vision by his word.

“He called upon the mighty Lord, when his enemies pressed upon him on every side, when he offered the sucking lamb. And the Lord thundered from heaven, and with a great noise made his voice to be heard. And he destroyed the rulers of the Tyrians, and all the princes of the Philistines.”

The sucking lamb, the thunder from heaven with a great noise, and the rulers of the Tyrians and all the princes of the Philistines destroyed: that is Samuel at Mizpeh.

“And after his death he prophesied, and shewed the king his end, and lifted up his voice from the earth in prophecy, to blot out the wickedness of the people.” He showed the king his end.

The Lord told Saul what was going to happen, that his kingdom was going to come to an end, and this was all done through the prophet Samuel. Give it up for our forefather Samuel.

precepts.why:
“Now there was a certain man of Ramathaim–zophim, of mount Ephraim, and his name was Elkanah, the son of Jeroham, the son of Elihu, the son of Tohu, the son of Zuph, an Ephrathite: And he had two wives; the name of the one was Hannah, and the name of the other Peninnah: and Peninnah had children, but Hannah had no children.”

“And this man went up out of his city yearly to worship and to sacrifice unto the Lord of hosts in Shiloh. And the two sons of Eli, Hophni and Phinehas, the priests of the Lord, were there.” Those are Eli's sons, and we remember how they were moving. “But unto Hannah he gave a worthy portion; for he loved Hannah: but the Lord had shut up her womb. And her adversary also provoked her sore, for to make her fret, because the Lord had shut up her womb.”

“And she was in bitterness of soul, and prayed unto the Lord, and wept sore. And she vowed a vow, and said, O Lord of hosts, if thou wilt indeed look on the affliction of thine handmaid, and remember me, and not forget thine handmaid, but wilt give unto thine handmaid a man child, then I will give him unto the Lord all the days of his life, and there shall no razor come upon his head.” Eli watched her and thought she was drunken, because “only her lips moved, but her voice was not heard.” Her answer: “No, my lord, I am a woman of a sorrowful spirit: I have drunk neither wine nor strong drink, but have poured out my soul before the Lord. Count not thine handmaid for a daughter of Belial: for out of the abundance of my complaint and grief have I spoken hitherto.” And Eli blessed it: “Go in peace: and the God of Israel grant thee thy petition that thou hast asked of him.”

Sometimes you have to go before the Lord and just let it go. That is what the sister did. She wanted seed. Sometimes life be life-ing, and everybody ain't capable, but you don't know what the Lord has in store. You ask the Lord, and if he chooses to give, he will. “and the Lord remembered her.”

“Wherefore it came to pass, when the time was come about after Hannah had conceived, that she bare a son, and called his name Samuel, saying, Because I have asked him of the Lord.” Then she kept her end of the bargain: “I will not go up until the child be weaned, and then I will bring him, that he may appear before the Lord, and there abide for ever.” She brought him with three bullocks and one ephah of flour and a bottle of wine to the house of the Lord in Shiloh, and said, “For this child I prayed; and the Lord hath given me my petition which I asked of him: Therefore also I have lent him to the Lord; as long as he liveth he shall be lent to the Lord.” She said, if I have a child, he's yours, and she kept it.

Understand the level of faith in this. “And Hannah prayed, and said, My heart rejoiceth in the Lord, mine horn is exalted in the Lord: my mouth is enlarged over mine enemies; because I rejoice in thy salvation. There is none holy as the Lord: for there is none beside thee: neither is there any rock like our God.”

“Talk no more so exceeding proudly; let not arrogancy come out of your mouth: for the Lord is a God of knowledge, and by him actions are weighed.” That is the context in which we use it. “The bows of the mighty men are broken, and they that stumbled are girded with strength. They that were full have hired out themselves for bread; and they that were hungry ceased: so that the barren hath born seven; and she that hath many children is waxed feeble.”

“The Lord killeth, and maketh alive: he bringeth down to the grave, and bringeth up. The Lord maketh poor, and maketh rich: he bringeth low, and lifteth up. He raiseth up the poor out of the dust, and lifteth up the beggar from the dunghill, to set them among princes, and to make them inherit the throne of glory: for the pillars of the earth are the Lord's, and he hath set the world upon them.”

“He will keep the feet of his saints, and the wicked shall be silent in darkness; for by strength shall no man prevail. The adversaries of the Lord shall be broken to pieces; out of heaven shall he thunder upon them: the Lord shall judge the ends of the earth; and he shall give strength unto his king, and exalt the horn of his anointed.” Shall be broken to pieces. That is a powerful prayer, and the sister was in the spirit. The Lord delivered as she asked, she kept her end of the bargain, and this man grew up to be a powerful prophet.
“And Samuel judged Israel all the days of his life.” He was the last one, and the reason is that after him came King Saul, and after that we went into kingship.

“And they arose early: and it came to pass about the spring of the day, that Samuel called Saul to the top of the house, saying, Up, that I may send thee away. And Saul arose, and they went out both of them, he and Samuel, abroad.”

“And as they were going down to the end of the city, Samuel said to Saul, Bid the servant pass on before us, (and he passed on,) but stand thou still a while, that I may shew thee the word of God.” He put the servant out of the way first, so he could show Saul the word of God.

“Then Samuel took a vial of oil, and poured it upon his head, and kissed him, and said, Is it not because the Lord hath anointed thee to be captain over his inheritance?” So you see he anointed Saul.

And he gave him the signs that would follow: “When thou art departed from me to day, then thou shalt find two men by Rachel's sepulchre in the border of Benjamin at Zelzah; and they will say unto thee, The asses which thou wentest to seek are found.” Then “thou shalt come to the plain of Tabor, and there shall meet thee three men going up to God to Beth–el, one carrying three kids, and another carrying three loaves of bread, and another carrying a bottle of wine: And they will salute thee, and give thee two loaves of bread; which thou shalt receive of their hands.”

This is the anointing of King David. “Then Samuel took the horn of oil, and anointed him in the midst of his brethren: and the Spirit of the Lord came upon David from that day forward. So Samuel rose up, and went to Ramah.”

“But the Spirit of the Lord departed from Saul, and an evil spirit from the Lord troubled him.” So you see David being anointed and the spirit coming upon him, and the spirit leaving Saul. Samuel was the one; he anointed both kings.

This is when he was a child, and Samuel heard God's voice. “And the child Samuel ministered unto the Lord before Eli. And the word of the Lord was precious in those days; there was no open vision. And it came to pass at that time, when Eli was laid down in his place, and his eyes began to wax dim, that he could not see; And ere the lamp of God went out in the temple of the Lord, where the ark of God was, and Samuel was laid down to sleep.”

“That the Lord called Samuel: and he answered, Here am I. And he ran unto Eli, and said, Here am I; for thou calledst me. And he said, I called not; lie down again.” It happened again, and a third time, “Now Samuel did not yet know the Lord, neither was the word of the Lord yet revealed unto him.” Then “Eli perceived that the Lord had called the child.” That is when Eli picked up what was going on, and he told him: “Go, lie down: and it shall be, if he call thee, that thou shalt say, Speak, Lord; for thy servant heareth.”

“And the Lord came, and stood, and called as at other times, Samuel, Samuel. Then Samuel answered, Speak; for thy servant heareth. And the Lord said to Samuel, Behold, I will do a thing in Israel, at which both the ears of every one that heareth it shall tingle. In that day I will perform against Eli all things which I have spoken concerning his house: when I begin, I will also make an end.” This is the Lord now speaking to Samuel. When you read the whole story, Samuel has to go and tell Eli what was said, and Eli knew exactly what time it was; he knew the evil that was going on in his house. Remember Eli's sons and how they were moving. It all came full circle here.

“And Samuel spake unto all the house of Israel, saying, If ye do return unto the Lord with all your hearts, then put away the strange gods and Ashtaroth from among you, and prepare your hearts unto the Lord, and serve him only: and he will deliver you out of the hand of the Philistines. Then the children of Israel did put away Baalim and Ashtaroth, and served the Lord only.”

“And Samuel said, Gather all Israel to Mizpeh, and I will pray for you unto the Lord. And they gathered together to Mizpeh, and drew water, and poured it out before the Lord, and fasted on that day, and said there, We have sinned against the Lord.” Then the Philistines came up, and Israel was afraid, and they said to Samuel, “Cease not to cry unto the Lord our God for us, that he will save us out of the hand of the Philistines.” They knew what time it was, because they knew they had been in the midst of sin and they were thinking judgment was coming.

“And Samuel took a sucking lamb, and offered it for a burnt offering wholly unto the Lord: and Samuel cried unto the Lord for Israel; and the Lord heard him. And as Samuel was offering up the burnt offering, the Philistines drew near to battle against Israel: but the Lord thundered with a great thunder on that day upon the Philistines, and discomfited them; and they were smitten before Israel.” That is exactly what Ecclesiasticus 46 was talking about: the sucking lamb, and the Lord thundering from heaven.

“And the men of Israel went out of Mizpeh, and pursued the Philistines, and smote them, until they came under Beth–car. Then Samuel took a stone, and set it between Mizpeh and Shen, and called the name of it Eben–ezer, saying, Hitherto hath the Lord helped us.” And then: “So the Philistines were subdued, and they came no more into the coast of Israel: and the hand of the Lord was against the Philistines all the days of Samuel.”

See how the prophets get to the root of the problem. He understood that the only way we are going to be able to fight is if we get rid of this sin amongst us and pray to the Most High for forgiveness. That is the only way it's going to happen.

This is when Samuel rebuked Saul and told him what was going to happen to his kingdom. “And Samuel said, Hath the Lord as great delight in burnt offerings and sacrifices, as in obeying the voice of the Lord? Behold, to obey is better than sacrifice, and to hearken than the fat of rams.”

To obey is better than sacrifice.

“For rebellion is as the sin of witchcraft, and stubbornness is as iniquity and idolatry. Because thou hast rejected the word of the Lord, he hath also rejected thee from being king.”

“And Saul said unto Samuel, I have sinned: for I have transgressed the commandment of the Lord, and thy words: because I feared the people, and obeyed their voice. Now therefore, I pray thee, pardon my sin, and turn again with me, that I may worship the Lord. And Samuel said unto Saul, I will not return with thee: for thou hast rejected the word of the Lord, and the Lord hath rejected thee from being king over Israel.”

“And as Samuel turned about to go away, he laid hold upon the skirt of his mantle, and it rent. And Samuel said unto him, The Lord hath rent the kingdom of Israel from thee this day, and hath given it to a neighbour of thine, that is better than thou.” A neighbour of thine that is better than thou: that is David. The Lord told him what was going to happen, that his kingdom was going to come to an end, and it was all done through the prophet Samuel.
